clue.text: Be far too improper, not wearing shoes or socks

indicators.note: improper means not in the right form, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A scold telling someone they are behaving far too badly by going about with bare feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Being barefoot means having the feet uncovered, with no footwear of any kind.

clue.text: See second child slide sideways

parts.note: a kid is an informal word for a child

explanation.surface: An instruction to watch a younger sibling sliding across the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is when a vehicle or person slips sideways out of control, a synonym in verb form.

clue.text: Female, not so young, may hide loose papers

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun: the thing that may hide papers

parts.note: someone not so young is older

explanation.surface: An older woman might be tucking away some stray documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A folder is a card cover in which loose sheets are kept together and out of sight.

clue.text: Please don't blow your own musical instrument!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: from the idiom 'blow your own ...', to boast

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense completes the idiom about boasting; the second is the literal brass instrument you do blow.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'blow your own trumpet' means to brag, and the trumpet is also a brass wind instrument.

clue.text: River theatre: what boos it evokes!

indicators.note: evokes means calls something forth, here calling out a new word from the letters of the preceding pair

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A floating playhouse on a river, and the jeers it draws from its audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A showboat is a paddle steamer carrying a theatre troupe that performed in towns along American rivers.

clue.text: Authorised to walk briskly with independent friend

parts.note: to leg it is slang for to walk or run off quickly
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone given permission to stride off in the company of a free-spirited pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimate means sanctioned by law or proper authority, a synonym of authorised.

clue.text: Cheat — one does this with lodgers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to deceive or swindle
second meaning: to accept paying guests into one's home

explanation.walkthrough: The dash separates two unrelated senses of one phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone in is to fool them, and taking in lodgers is housing them for rent.

clue.text: Secret way into the garden?

parts.note: a figurative covert route into something
literally, the rear door of a house that opens onto the garden

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: the rear door of a house leads into the garden, while the phrase also means an underhand route.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a rear entrance to a house and an unofficial, hidden means of access.

clue.text: Cutting into scratchy enamel, I'm sometimes laughing

definitions.note: the animal speaking of itself, so it stands for the noun

indicators.note: the answer cuts into the run of letters across the two words, sitting inside them

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A scratched coat of enamel being cut into, with a giggle on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena is known as the laughing hyena for its cackling call.

clue.text: This legal document can be read two ways

parts.note: a formal signed and sealed instrument in law
the four letters run the same forwards and backwards

explanation.surface: A lawyer pointing out that a contract is ambiguous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read two ways' suggests ambiguous wording, but it means the word reads the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is a signed and sealed legal instrument, such as one transferring property.

clue.text: Tongue-tied restaurant employee who moves things around

definitions.note: describes the thing: one that moves things around

parts.note: tongue-tied means unable to speak, i.e. dumb
a waiter serves at tables in a restaurant

explanation.surface: A silent waiter shuffling plates about the dining room.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads like a description of a shy waiter, but the answer is a machine, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumbwaiter is a small lift carrying food and dishes between floors, or a revolving serving stand.

clue.text: More sheltered lettuce that is found by the river

parts.note: cos is a variety of long-leaved lettuce
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A garden note that lettuces grown near water do better out of the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosier means snugger and more protected, comparative to match 'more sheltered'.

clue.text: Many on line will get scrambled as a mere formality

indicators.note: scrambled means mixed up, so the letters of the preceding words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that lots of people going online will get their data jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held in name only is nominal, existing as a title or formality without real substance.

clue.text: The first of empty gestures, like love and fear

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: the word supplying its initial
motions are movements or gestures

explanation.surface: Hollow gestures standing in for real feelings such as love and fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Love and fear are examples of strong feelings, the category the answer names.

clue.text: Study, eg Brazil, having to turn back, which is senseless

indicators.note: turning back means the combined words are read from the end to the start

parts.note: a den is a private room for study
Brazil nuts are an example of nuts

explanation.surface: A study of Brazil forced into a U-turn, which seems pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: Brazil looks like the country, but it is the nut.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stunned is to be knocked unconscious or dazed, without one's senses.

clue.text: I left the party, always going outside to get a sinner

indicators.note: the word for always wraps around the other pieces, going outside them

parts.note: ever means always
taken as written
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone who quit the party and keeps stepping outside, branded a sinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An evildoer is a person who commits wicked acts, a synonym of sinner.

clue.text: Ship's guide going round in the morning

indicators.note: the word for guide goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to steer is to guide
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, in the morning

explanation.surface: A ship's pilot making the rounds in the early hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a steam-powered vessel, a type of ship.

clue.text: Get Humpty Dumpty, perhaps, to sow a moussaka ingredient

parts.note: Humpty Dumpty of the nursery rhyme is drawn as an egg
to sow is to plant

explanation.surface: A nonsense instruction to get the nursery rhyme egg sowing a Greek dish ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggplant is the American name for aubergine, layered into the Greek baked dish moussaka.

clue.text: Sorry to be a copy editor?

parts.note: taken as written
a sham is a fake or imitation

explanation.surface: Someone apologising for being merely a sub-editor, or a plagiarising one.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as A SHAM ED, a fake editor; ED is the standard abbreviation for editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling ashamed means feeling regret and embarrassment, close to being sorry.

clue.text: Bishop's outfit helps female servers

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
an arm is a branch or unit of an organisation, an outfit
aids means helps

explanation.surface: A bishop's vestments being of use to the women who wait on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outfit' suggests clothing, but here it means an organisation, of which ARM is a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmaids are women who serve drinks behind a bar.

clue.text: Such discrimination is used to cut a stone

indicators.note: the small word cuts into the other pieces, sitting inside them

parts.note: taken as written
a gem is a precious stone
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gem cutter remarking on a type of prejudice applied to stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is prejudice or unfair treatment on the grounds of a person's age.

clue.text: Nice wage, not starting in very cold weather

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its starting letter

parts.note: the word loses its starting letter
this word too loses its starting letter, under the same instruction

explanation.surface: A decent salary that never begins to arrive during a bitter freeze.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice age is a long period of glaciation, an extreme of cold climate.

clue.text: Actually, I need to keep an old penny

indicators.note: the first words keep the penny within them, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written
d was the symbol for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they really do need to save an old coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an adverb meaning in fact or truly, just as actually does.

clue.text: Repeated promise of partnership is not new

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it, repeating the proposal; a second time is a repeat
a hand, as in asking for someone's hand in marriage

explanation.surface: A proposal of marriage made a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods have had a previous owner, so they are used rather than fresh.

clue.text: Head of house gets everyone together in this large room

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the word supplying its initial
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A head of household gathering the family in the big room.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall is a spacious room for meetings or gatherings.

clue.text: Triumphant cry for chopped ham, presented twice

indicators.note: the shortened piece is given two times in a row
a chopped word has its end cut off

parts.note: the meat word, used for both copies
the same meat word again, chopped the same way

explanation.surface: A cook gloating over sliced ham served up two times.
explanation.definitionFit: Ha-ha is an exclamation of glee or mockery at someone else's misfortune.

clue.text: Healing ointment very obtainable in a sale

indicators.note: the abbreviation is to be found inside the word for sale

parts.note: a sale here is the word sale itself

explanation.surface: A soothing cream that is very easy to pick up at a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A salve is a soothing ointment applied to wounds or sores.

clue.text: It has a thick skin, which is more flexible than peel

indicators.note: something flexible can be bent into new shapes, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A comparison of some thick rind with fruit peel for pliability.
explanation.definitionFit: The elephant is a pachyderm, literally a thick-skinned animal.
